conventions.convention: Q(v)=B(v,v), Clifford generators satisfy v²=Q(v)1, and real signature (p,q) means p positive and q negative squares. Reflection and group results require a finite-dimensional nondegenerate real form.
Clifford conjugation is reversion composed with grading, so conjugation sends v to −v. The norm is N(x)=x conjugate(x), giving N(u)=−Q(u).
The twisted action is ρ_x(v)=α(x)vx⁻¹. Pin is generated by vectors with |Q(u)|=1 in positive dimension; Pin(0)={1,−1}. Full-even Spin is Pin∩Cl⁰, whereas norm-one Spin additionally requires N(x)=1.
A real Clifford spinor representation means a restriction of a finite-dimensional unital even-Clifford module, rather than an arbitrary representation of the Spin group.
Pin and Spin carry the subspace topology of the finite-dimensional real Clifford algebra; orthogonal groups carry their matrix topology.

Complete reducibility concerns continuous finite-dimensional complex representations and assumes AC through the compact-group supplier. The universal-cover corollary also assumes AC, through the numerable-bundle fibration theorem, and asserts universality only for n≥3.
In the positive plane E=e₁e₂, a lift of the standard rotation by θ is cos(θ/2)−E sin(θ/2). Positive-square chirality is iE, and its two half-spin characters are a−ib and a+ib.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite-dimensional nondegenerate real quadratic space, anisotropic u acts by its reflection. Every unrestricted twisted normalizer acts orthogonally, is homogeneous, and is a nonzero scalar times an anisotropic-vector product. The twisted-action kernel is exactly the nonzero real scalars.

Every orthogonal transformation of a finite-dimensional nondegenerate real quadratic space is a product of at most dim V anisotropic reflections. The parity is even exactly for special orthogonal transformations.
N is scalar-valued and multiplicative on Γ; on anisotropic-vector products it equals the product of −Q(u_j). Pin has the norm-±1 characterization, and its even subgroup is full-even Spin.
Pin→O(V,B) and full-even Spin→SO(V,B) are exact central extensions with kernel {1,−1}. Both groups are compact for definite forms.
There is an identity neighborhood U in SO(V,B) and a continuous section s:U→Spin_N=1 with s(I)=1 and ρ(s(A))=A.
With the specified finite-dimensional topologies, the Pin and full-even Spin action maps are continuous central two-sheeted covering maps.
For n≥2, Spin_full(n)→Sⁿ⁻¹, x↦ρ_x(e_n), is a locally trivial right Spin_full(n−1) bundle, with explicit rotor sections and a finite partition of unity whose closed supports lie within chart domains.

The real span of full-even Spin is Cl⁰. For Cl⁰ isomorphic to a product of M_rj(D_j), its irreducible real Clifford spinor restrictions are the column modules D_j^rj, with real dimensions r_j dim_R D_j and commutants D_j opposite.

concerns.concern: Proof 1.1 chooses an orthogonal anisotropic basis e_i and introduces normalized vectors u_i separately. Proof 2.1 then says “Set ω=i^m e_1⋯e_{2m}; the Clifford relations show ω²=1” and constructs p_±=(1±ω)/2. For the basis actually chosen, ω²=∏Q(e_i), which need not equal 1. In dimension two, take e_1=2f_1 and e_2=f_2 for an orthonormal basis f_i: ω²=4, so the asserted p_± are not idempotents. The theorem's decomposition remains plausible, but this computation requires an explicitly orthonormal basis or the normalized u_i.
The Remarks locate the replacement real-polynomial selection argument in “step 1.2”; that argument is actually in step 1.3. Step 1.2 treats an anisotropic fixed vector.
